::: {#thm-pearson-r-range}
#### Range of the correlation coefficient

The Pearson correlation coefficient satisfies $-1 \le r \le 1$.
Moreover, $r = 1$ if and only if the points $(x_i, y_i)$
lie on a straight line with positive slope,
and $r = -1$ if and only if they lie on a straight line with negative slope.
:::

::: proof

Write $a_i \eqdef x_i - \bar x$ and $b_i \eqdef y_i - \bar y$,
so that $r = \sum_i a_i b_i / \paren{\sqrt{\sum_i a_i^2} \sqrt{\sum_i b_i^2}}$.
The Cauchy--Schwarz inequality states that
$\abs{\sum_i a_i b_i} \le \sqrt{\sum_i a_i^2} \sqrt{\sum_i b_i^2}$,
with equality if and only if one of the vectors
$(a_1, \ldots, a_n)$ and $(b_1, \ldots, b_n)$
is a scalar multiple of the other.
Dividing both sides by the (positive) right-hand side gives $\abs{r} \le 1$.

Equality $\abs{r} = 1$ therefore holds
if and only if $b_i = c \, a_i$ for some constant $c \ne 0$ and every $i$,
that is, $y_i = \bar y + c(x_i - \bar x)$:
the points lie on a line with slope $c$.
Then $\sum_i a_i b_i = c \sum_i a_i^2$ has the sign of $c$,
so $r = 1$ when $c > 0$ and $r = -1$ when $c < 0$.

:::
